entries.detail: Not in papers/ and not openly available. ResearchGate returned HTTP 403 / Cloudflare to WebFetch and curl with a browser user-agent (2026-09-25 verification, repeated later) and was skipped in the 2026-10-10 network pass (login). Card R9 rests on a search snippet only. A web search for the 2004 study found nothing (TRC hits were unrelated Opunake Power hydro consents). Authors and report number are not confirmed. This is the most likely source of the reef position, design plan and dimensions.

entries.what: LINZ open aerial imagery of Opunake cove, 2011-12 (0.4 m) and 2021-22 (0.25 m), tile BJ28_5000_0806
entries.by: agent: Opunake network pass (fresh agent, cloud)
entries.detail: Crops of 1 km viewed once each (registry opunake-reef-img-11, img-12). 2011-12 (flown 2011-11-30 to 2012-03-30): clear water, curved wave lines peeling from the north headland and one whitewater patch, no bag field or pale rectangle. 2021-22 (flown 2021-11-23 to 2022-01-07): darker, rougher water, no structure. The reef is submerged, so not seeing it is not evidence that it is absent. Other LINZ sets exist (1976-2002 film scans, 2016-18 0.3 m, 2022-23 0.1 m, tiles BJ28_500_*) and were not fetched or not found for this tile.
entries.might_work: Google Earth Pro history 2007-2010 (Lior: G8), when the bags were fresh

entries.by: agent: Opunake network pass (fresh agent, cloud)
entries.detail: All 197 releases were scanned for the z19 tile: 173 have a tile here, 4 distinct versions by MD5 (registry opunake-reef-img-13 to img-16). A contrast-stretched crop of the water showed no bags in any of them. Capture dates were not retrieved (release dates only).

entries.what: Esri World Imagery z20 around -39.4577, 173.8545 (capture date 2025-01-16, 0.115 m/px)
entries.detail: Viewed once at 1100 px (registry opunake-reef-img-07 to img-10): shows the NW headland, boulder foreshore, surf-zone whitewater, wet black sand at low tide, camping ground and township. No bag field and no regular pale or dark rectangle. Bags are submerged and the water is turbid, so absence in the image is not evidence that the reef is absent. The image window is centred on -39.4577, 173.8545, which is itself a guess.

entries.what: papers/ folder: any plan figure, coordinates or crest datum for Opunake in Lior's 5 PDFs
entries.detail: Opunake appears only in text and tables: Mead and Borrero 2011 p.1 (Fig 1 world map) and p.3-4 (s.3.1.5: 4,800 m3, start 2006, last work May 2008, 1,400 m3 short, no drawing); Rendle 2016 thesis Table 2.1 (p.41) and references (p.298); Blacka et al. 2013 Tables 4.1-4.4 (30 m x 100 m, depth 1.8-3.0 m, about 300 m offshore, A$0.93M) and references. Those facts are card references; the plan, position and datum part failed. The 2007 Mount Maunganui paper has no usable text layer (image pages, not OCR'd) and the 2023 Narrowneck paper has no Opunake mention.
